Their research supervision during this period focuses on the intersection of digital environments and social behaviors, specifically through the lenses of arts and creative practice and social media. Based on the available data, they have supervised two students, Dasha Elisa T. Lariosa and Ciphia May D. Molina. The repository contains no articles authored by Sarmiento, and there is no information regarding their specific academic degrees, institutional affiliations, or professional awards.

In terms of research focus, Sarmiento has supervised studies that examine how digital content influences attitudes and actions. One supervised thesis, "Sining Para sa Pagbabago: Examining How Sharing Protest Art Online Shapes the Attitudes and Actions of Young Filipinos Towards Socio-Political Advocacy Groups" (2025), investigates the transition of protest art from physical to digital spaces. This work, supervised for student Dasha Elisa T. Lariosa, explores how sharing such art online affects the attitudes and actions of young Filipinos toward socio-political advocacy groups. The research utilizes grounded theory and focuses on themes of digital activism and online spaces. A second supervised thesis, "Exploring Influences of Pet-Related Social Media Content on Perceptions of Pet Adoption" (2025), supervised for student Ciphia May D. Molina, examines how social media content affects the attitudes and intentions of pet owners and non-owners toward pet adoption within Metro Manila. This indicates a research interest in how social media content shapes specific social perceptions and intentions.

There is no information available regarding their specific methodology preferences beyond the use of grounded theory in one instance, nor is there data concerning their long-term career trajectory or specific academic expertise in these fields.
